claims.text: Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr is a refractory high-entropy alloy suitable for temperature-dependent plastic-deformation applications.
Annealing Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr at 600–700 °C for 10–50 hours produces an inverted microstructure.
The inverted microstructure consists of discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix.
The as-processed or slowly cooled target alloy has a continuous B2 phase containing cuboidal BCC pockets.
A controlled atmosphere is required during the intermediate-temperature annealing.
Controlled cooling after annealing preserves the refined inverted microstructure.
The annealing treatment tunes phase fractions and precipitate sizes.
Changes in phase fractions and precipitate sizes alter dislocation pathways.
Improved dislocation interactions produce greater elevated-temperature strength and better room-temperature ductility.
An inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves room-temperature compressive ductility relative to a continuous-B2 microstructure.
An inverted BCC+B2 microstructure can maintain high yield strength at both room and elevated temperatures.
The annealed target alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the unannealed alloy.
The annealed target alloy will maintain or slightly improve ambient-temperature ductility relative to the unannealed alloy.
Two-phase B2+BCC refractory high-entropy alloys typically exhibit high yield strength but poor room-temperature ductility.
The poor room-temperature ductility of these alloys is attributed to a continuous ordered-B2 matrix.
The beneficial outcome is restricted to annealing at 600–700 °C for 10–50 hours and to the stated alloy composition.
Departures from the specified temperature, duration, or composition may prevent formation of the inverted microstructure or balanced mechanical properties.
The quantitative strength and ductility improvements and exact phase distribution remain to be validated.
